latin: In Garamantum<sup>1</sup> sōlitūdine dēstitūtus jacuī. Frāctum erat aliquid in compāgibus<sup>2</sup> illīs quae māchinam movēbant.
Cum autem nec artificem<sup>3</sup> nec peregrīnātōrēs ūllōs mēcum veherem, ita mē parāvī ut<sup>4</sup> sōlus id arte reficere cōnārer.
Rēs quidem<sup>5</sup> difficilis erat, sed in discrīmen vītae<sup>6</sup> adductus eram.
Tantum enim aquae habēbam quantum<sup>7</sup> ad pōtum octo diērum satis esset. ...
... Cum Rēgulō cōnsuētūdinem jūnxī.
Tempus multum intercessit<sup>8</sup> priusquam<sup>9</sup> intellegerem unde is venīret.
Rēgulus enim, ut ex mē multa percontābātur<sup>10</sup>, sīc percontantem mē audīre nōn vidēbātur.
Vōcibus fortuitō missīs omnia paulātim comperī<sup>11</sup>.

Velut<sup>12</sup>, cum prīmum volucrem<sup>13</sup> māchinam cōnspexit (quam māchinam nōn dēscrībam: fōrma enim ejus adeō est multiplex ut<sup>14</sup> eam dēlīneāre nōn possim) ā mē quaesīvit<sup>15</sup>:
Rēgulus. — Quidnam reī hoc est?
Antōnius. — Haec nōn rēs est — volat enim — sed volucris quaedam, mea volucris māchinā.
Et superbiā efferēbar dum<sup>16</sup> eum mē volāre doceō.
Reg. — Quid? Dē caelō dēlāpsus es<sup>17</sup>?
Ant., summissē. — Ita est.
latinAccented: In Garamántum<sup>1</sup> sōlitū́dine dēstitū́tus jácuī. Frāctum erat áliquid in compā́gibus<sup>2</sup> illīs quae mā́chinam movḗbant.
Cum autem nec artíficem<sup>3</sup> nec peregrīnātṓrēs ūllōs mēcum véherem, ita mē parā́vī ut<sup>4</sup> sōlus id arte refícere cōnā́rer.
Rēs quidem<sup>5</sup> diffícilis erat, sed in discrī́men vītae<sup>6</sup> addúctus eram.
Tantum enim aquae habḗbam quantum<sup>7</sup> ad pōtum octo diḗrum satis esset. ...
... Cum Rḗgulō cōnsuētū́dinem jūnxī.
Tempus multum intercéssit<sup>8</sup> priúsquam<sup>9</sup> intellégerem unde is venī́ret.
Rḗgulus enim, ut ex mē multa percontābā́tur<sup>10</sup>, sīc percontántem mē audī́re nōn vidēbā́tur.
Vṓcibus fortúitō missīs ómnia paulā́tim cómperī<sup>11</sup>.

Velut<sup>12</sup>, cum prīmum vólucrem<sup>13</sup> mā́chinam cōnspéxit (quam mā́chinam nōn dēscrī́bam: fōrma enim ejus ádeō est múltiplex ut<sup>14</sup> eam dēlīneā́re nōn possim) ā mē quaesī́vit<sup>15</sup>:
Rḗgulus. — Quidnam reī hoc est?
Antṓnius. — Haec nōn rēs est — volat enim — sed vólucris quaedam, mea vólucris mā́chinā.
Et supérbiā efferḗbar dum<sup>16</sup> eum mē volā́re dóceō.
Reg. — Quid? Dē caelō dēlā́psus es<sup>17</sup>?
Ant., summíssē. — Ita est.
english: I [had broken down] (lay abandoned) in the desert [of the Garamantes] (of the Sahara). Something had broken [in the mechanism] (those organs) which made the machine work.
But as I was carrying neither mechanic nor passenger(s) with me, I prepared myself (so that) [to try] (I tried) [to repair] this [alone] (to remake by art).
The thing was certainly difficult, but I was [led into] [mortal danger] (trial of life).
In fact [I had just enough water for eight days] (so much of water I had as much as for drink of eight days enough was)...
... I made friends with the little prince.
A lot of time passed before I understood where he came from.
The little prince in fact, while he asked me many things (thus me asking), did not seem to hear [my questions].
[It was] by words dropped by chance [that] little by little I discovered everything.
Thus, when he looked for the first time at my plane, (this machine, I will not represent it: its shape in fact is so complicated that I would not know how to draw it) he asked me:
The little prince. — [What is that thing] (what then of thing this is)?
Antoine. — It's not a thing — [it] flies — it's a plane, my plane.
And I was [proud] (carried by pride) [to teach him] (while I teach him) that I flew.
Prince. — What! You fell from the sky?
Antoine, modestly. — Yes.

footnotes: Garamantes, -um, m. pl., people living in the Sahara.
Compages, -is, f., or compago, -inis, f., assembly, articulation.
Artifex, -icis, m., means at the same time artist, artisan, or even worker: the man of art (ars, artis).
Ita... ut + subj., in such a way that.
Quidem, adv., certainly, assuredly; ne... quidem, not even.

Discrimen, -inis, n., distance, separation, distinction; figuratively: trial, danger. In discrimen vitae (in + acc., for adductus gives an idea of MOVEMENT). Danger of death is said in Latin: «danger of life» (likewise, in German, Lebensgefahr).
Quantum aquae?, how much water?; tantum aquae, so much water; tantum... quantum, as much as; here: enough for.
Intercedere, to advance between: another compound of cedere!

Priusquam and antequam govern the subjunctive each time the idea to be expressed goes beyond the simple relation of anteriority. The second verb, veniret, is also in the subjunctive because it is an INDIRECT QUESTION.

Percontari, deponent verb, to ask. If the present participle percontantem worries you, it is because you need to look at R. and N. 28, 3 B again. Note also, in this phrase 7, sic... ut, in the same way as; but the two terms are inverted and mark an opposition.
Comperio, -is, -ire, peri, pertum, to discover, to learn, to recognize.

Velut, conj. (vel, ut), at the beginning of a sentence, means: thus, for example; but its most frequent sense is: in the same way as. It is often met with sic or ita: velut... sic..., in the same way as... so...; or with si: velut si..., as if...
Volucer, f. volucris, n. volucre (3rd decl., gen. in cris for the three genders), which flies.

In case you have forgotten it, we remind you of quaero, -is, -ere, quaesivi or quaesii, quaesitum. Quaerere rem ab aliquo, to ask something of someone. Quaeso is conjugated in the same way (-is, -ere, ivi or ii, itum) but is only used in a few expressions such as dic, quaeso!, say, I beg you!
Dum, meaning while, is construed with the present indicative, even if it is a past fact.
Delapsus es, perfect of delabi, which is conjugated like labi, to slide.
comments: Latus, -eris, n., the side; think of LATERAL. — Metrum unum longus: measure is expressed by the accusative, unless one insists on the idea of SEPARATION or DISTANCE; e.g.: urbes ambae 20 kilometris distant, the two towns are 20 km apart. — You should have found for yourself: longitudo, -inis, f.; brevis, -is, -e, adj.; mango, -onis, m., merchant, horse dealer. Several names of professions are in o, -onis; you have already seen caupo and centurio.
Do you always think of learning the names of numbers (titles of lessons, page numbers, and indications at the bottom of right-hand pages)?

latin: Quōmodo āream rectangūlī computāmus?
Sufficit mēnsūram majōris ejus lateris per minōris mēnsūram multiplicāre.
Bene! Sit, ē.g. (exemplī grātia) rectangulus quīdam metrum ūnum longus, trīgintā centimetra latus; quanta erit, dīc, āreā ejus?
Prīmum oportet ut haec duo latera ūna atque eadem longitūdinis ratiōne commētiāmur.
Ē.g., mihi dīcere licet rectangulum tuum decimetrā decem longum, tria lātum esse.
Cum ter dēnā sint trīgintā, āreā ejus est decimetra quadrāta trīgintā...
Equus conductīcius facit brevia mīlia.
Quid est equus conductīcius?
Is est quem mangō tibi prō pecūniā commodāvit, vel, sī vīs, quem tū ā mangōne condūxistī.
Cūr brevia mīlia?
Quia eques equum suum proprium amat et bene cūrat, aliēnum autem vēlōciter currentem dēfatīgāre nōn dubitat.
Sī ita agit, licet cum equō aliēnō, pessimus est eques.
latinAccented: Quṓmodo ā́ream rectangū́lī computā́mus?
Súfficit mēnsū́ram majṓris ejus láteris per minṓris mēnsū́ram multiplicā́re.
Bene! Sit, ē.g. (exémplī grā́tia) rectángulus quīdam metrum ūnum longus, trīgíntā centímetra latus; quanta erit, dīc, ā́reā ejus?
Prīmum opórtet ut haec duo látera ūna atque éadem longitū́dinis ratiṓne commētiā́mur.
Ē.g., mihi dī́cere licet rectángulum tuum decímetrā decem longum, tria lātum esse.
Cum ter dēnā sint trīgíntā, ā́reā ejus est decímetra quadrā́ta trīgíntā...
Equus conductī́cius facit brévia mī́lia.
Quid est equus conductī́cius?
Is est quem mangō tibi prō pecū́niā commodā́vit, vel, sī vīs, quem tū ā mangṓne condūxístī.
Cūr brévia mī́lia?
Quia eques equum suum próprium amat et bene cūrat, aliḗnum autem vēlṓciter curréntem dēfatīgā́re nōn dúbitat.
Sī ita agit, licet cum equō aliḗnō, péssimus est eques.
english: How do we calculate the area of a rectangle?
It is enough to multiply the measure of the (longer) [larger] side by the measure of the (shorter) [smaller].
Good! [Suppose], for example, a rectangle of 1 m (in) length and 30 cm (in) width; [tell me what] its surface will be?
First we must measure these two sides with one and the same [unit] (system) of length.
Thus, I may say that your rectangle is 10 dm long and 3 wide.
As 3 times 10 [make] (are) 30, its area is 30 square decimetres.
A hired horse [runs fast] (makes short miles).
What is a hired horse?
It is the one which the dealer has lent you for money, or if you like, which you have hired from the dealer.
Why short miles?
Because the rider loves and looks after well his own horse, but does not hesitate to exhaust [another man's horse] by making it run fast.
If he acts thus, even with another man's horse, he is a [very bad] rider.
